title: Spread density of an open in ordinary fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $W\subset X$ an open subset, and $\eta$ a point with closure all of $T$. For the scheme fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and their canonical maps $i_t:X_t\to X$, suppose $i_\eta^{-1}(W)$ is dense in $X_\eta$. Then there is an open $U\subset T$ containing $\eta$ such that $i_t^{-1}(W)$ is dense in $X_t$ for every $t\in U$. Density means that the topological closure is the entire fibre; empty fibres are allowed. No geometric irreducibility is assumed, and the conclusion concerns ordinary residue-field fibres only.

source.place: Tag 054X, Lemma 37.24.3, applied to the closed complement of an open subset; Tags 03HV and 054U in its proof.

proof.text: Give the closed complement Z = X \ W its reduced induced scheme structure. The generic density hypothesis says Z_eta is nowhere dense in X_eta. Reduce T and base change X and Z; the reduction map and its base changes are universal homeomorphisms, so all fibrewise topological density assertions are unchanged. The reduced irreducible base is integral. Apply generic flat finite presentation to X and Z and intersect the two resulting nonempty base opens. Each contains the generic point.

Follow Tag 054X on this common open. If Z_t has nonempty interior in X_t, take the generic point xi of a fibre component contained in that interior. Flatness of Z lifts the generalization eta of t to xi_prime in Z_eta (Tag 03HV). Apply Tag 054U to X and Z along xi_prime specializing to xi: xi is a generic point of a component in both fibres, and their fibre dimensions at xi agree. Their generic fibre dimensions at xi_prime therefore agree. A component of Z_eta through xi_prime has the dimension of X_eta there, contradicting nowhere density of Z_eta in the finite type scheme over the field kappa(eta). Hence Z_t has empty interior in each fibre.

The fibrewise complement of Z_t is i_t inverse image W and is open dense. Transport the common base open back through the reduction homeomorphism. This gives the required open containing eta. If a fibre is empty, its empty subset is dense and the conclusion holds as well.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_open_fibre_dense_of_generic_dense {X T : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (W : X.Opens) (η : T) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (hdense : Dense ((f.fiberι η) ⁻¹' (W : Set X))) :
    ∃ U : T.Opens, η ∈ U ∧
      ∀ (t : T), t ∈ U → Dense ((f.fiberι t) ⁻¹' (W : Set X))
